why_them: Three of our Vienna entries stand in the Schönbrunn botanical garden: the Ginkgo of Schönbrunn (vie_004), the Pedunculate Oak near the Hietzinger Tor (vie_021) and the Yew beside it (vie_022), and none of the three has a photograph.

org: Österreichische Bundesgärten (Bundesgärten Wien, Schönbrunn and Burggarten)
why_them: They are the actual gardeners of the Schönbrunn botanical garden trees we publish (vie_004, vie_021, vie_022), so they can confirm the age estimates for the Schönbrunn ginkgo that our sources disagree on.

org: Stiftung Preußische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin-Brandenburg (SPSG)
why_them: SPSG manages both Schlosspark Charlottenburg (the Swamp Cypress ber_004 and the Karpfenteich Elm ber_018) and Pfaueninsel, where five of our Berlin trees stand including the Türeiche and the Cut-Leaf Oak, whose species identification our own file already flags as contested.

org: Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques de la Ville de Genève
why_them: The Botanical Garden Plane Trees on the central avenue by the chemin de l'Impératrice (gen_004) are theirs, and they hold the planting records that would date the avenue precisely.

Their own yearbook archive is what let us corroborate a Copenhagen tree back to 1941 during research; they are the people most likely to correct or date the Assistens Kirkegård handkerchief tree (cop_006) and the Proviantgarden mulberry (cop_001).

Two of our New York entries are theirs, the Sassafras of Green-Wood (nyc_004) and the Second Camperdown Elm at Garden Path and Pink Avenue (nyc_014), and they run their own tree tours so they know exactly which specimens we got wrong.

We publish the Kansas Hawthorn across from their Lily Pool (nyc_015) and the Caucasian Wingnut north of the Rock Garden (nyc_016); both are garden-accessioned trees whose planting dates BBG holds and we could not find online.

Their Champion Trees of DC work overlaps directly with our fourteen Washington entries, including the Montrose Park Tulip Poplar (wdc_011) and the Battery Kemble Chestnut Oak (wdc_003), where we have honest but approximate pins they could sharpen.
The Dumbarton Oaks Beech Grove by the Lovers' Lane gate (wdc_014) is inside the park they steward, and we have no photograph of it at all.
Montrose Park and Dumbarton Oaks Park, home to two of our DC trees (wdc_011, wdc_014), sit inside the Rock Creek Park unit they work across, and their volunteer stewards walk those slopes weekly.

They train the Citizen Pruners who look after New York street trees, which is exactly the audience for our twenty-tree New York walk, and their volunteers stand next to the Hangman's Elm (nyc_001) more often than we ever will.

Their National Champion Tree register is a source we lean on for the Chicago champions (the Champion Boxelder chi_004 and the Champion Red Pine chi_005), and both entries would be stronger with their current measurements.

The Bur Oak Grove of Wooded Island in Jackson Park (chi_002) and the Bur Oak on the Midway (chi_001) are on their land, and Chicago is the thinnest of our US pages at six trees, so their oak inventory would decide whether it grows.

Five of our fourteen Munich trees stand in Schlosspark Nymphenburg: the Oak of the Dörfchen (muc_007), the Copper Beech and the Leaning Lime at the Badenburg (muc_011, muc_012), the Fern-leaved Beech at the Amalienburg (muc_013) and the Weeping Beech at the Schwanenbrücke (muc_014).

They tend the three Englischer Garten trees we publish: the Beech near Forstweg (muc_004), the Twin Elms by the Chinese Tower (muc_005) and the Fern-leaved Beech on the Schwabinger Bach (muc_006), all three still without a photograph.

The Röth-Linde at Gut Nederling (muc_001), the Krüner Eiche (muc_002) and the Reichs- und Friedenseiche in the Flaucheranlagen (muc_003) are municipal trees on their books, and they hold the Baumkataster entries that would confirm our age estimates.

Most of our twenty-two Vienna trees are theirs, including the Naturdenkmal planes of the Volksgarten (vie_007) and Rathauspark (vie_006) and the Field Elm on the Burggasse median (vie_018), which is a rare surviving elm they replant around.
They run Berlin's large public green sites and would know the current condition of the Great Elm of Treptower Park (ber_005), an elm-disease survivor we publish with an approximate pin.
They campaign on veteran trees nationally and their Berlin members are the likeliest people to have photographed Dicke Marie in Tegel (ber_001), Berlin's oldest tree and one of our photo gaps.

org: Kuratorium Baum des Jahres / Dr. Silvius Wodarz Stiftung
why_them: Their species-of-the-year work maps onto our species pages, and our Berlin list carries two European White Elms (ber_005, ber_018), the tree of the year they campaigned hardest on.

Six of our ten Boston trees are theirs, among them the Peters Hill White Oak (bos_002), the original 1948 Dawn Redwood by the Hunnewell Visitor Center (bos_005) and the Larz Anderson Hinoki Cypress bonsai (bos_007); their accession records are the definitive source for all six.

org: City of Boston Parks and Recreation Department
why_them: The Shaw Memorial Elms on Boston Common (bos_001) and the Dawn Redwood in the Public Garden (bos_004) are their trees, and both are English elms and a redwood whose survival they actively manage.
They fund the tree care on Boston Common and the Public Garden, so the Shaw Memorial Elms (bos_001) and the Public Garden Dawn Redwood (bos_004) are literally what their donors pay for.

org: The Morton Arboretum (Plant Clinic / Chicago Region Trees Initiative)
why_them: They run the Chicago Region Trees Initiative and the Illinois Big Tree Register, which is the source that gave us the Champion Boxelder of Edgebrook (chi_004) and the Champion Red Pine of Indian Boundary (chi_005), the only two city-limits records we could use.

Eight of our twenty New York trees stand in Central Park, including the Black Tupelo of the Ramble (nyc_002), the Elms on the Rocks by Literary Walk (nyc_012) and the Cedar of Lebanon grove near Conservatory Water (nyc_017); their arborists hold the tree data behind every one.

Stockholm is our thinnest Nordic page at four trees, and their arborist members are exactly who can tell us whether Birger Jarl's Oak at the Kristineberg interchange (sto_001) and Lyell's Oak at Fiskartorpet (sto_002) still hold the ages we published.

org: Bymiljøetaten, Oslo kommune (Oslo Agency for Urban Environment)
why_them: Munch-eika at Montebello (osl_001), the tree Edvard Munch painted, and the birches of Birkelunden (osl_003) are municipal trees they manage, and Oslo is a four-tree page we would like to grow with their register.

org: Statens Naturhistoriske Museum, Botanisk Have (University of Copenhagen)
why_them: The Ancient Cycad of the Palm House (cop_002), a Dioon edule that has been in the Palmehuset since the nineteenth century, is theirs, and it is the single hardest date in our Copenhagen page to verify.

They are the association of every Swiss municipal parks department, which is the fastest route to both our Swiss pages at once: the 1780 planes of Platzspitz (zur_001) and the Lindenhof limes (zur_003) in Zurich, and the Official Chestnut on the Promenade de la Treille (gen_001) in Geneva.

All four Zurich trees we publish are municipal, including Alfred Escher's Giant Sequoia in Belvoirpark (zur_002) and the Mammutbaum on Hohlstrasse (zur_004), and none of the four has a photograph. Their own site publishes only a web-support address (szh.egovservicedesk@zuerich.ch), so this is the department page rather than a verified mailbox.

org: NYC Parks (Department of Parks and Recreation)
why_them: Their forestry division holds the Great Trees of New York designations behind the Queens Giant (nyc_005), the Clove Lakes Colossus (nyc_007) and the Yew of Hero Park (nyc_008). Their site sits behind a bot challenge and publishes no address in the page source, so this is the contact page rather than a verified mailbox.

A long-running German tree-identification site with a reader community that photographs individual specimens, which is exactly the gap on our Berlin page where Dicke Marie (ber_001) and the Kaisereiche (ber_008) still have none. Address is Cloudflare-obfuscated on their own imprint and decoded from the raw HTML.
They catalogue German veteran trees by name and region, and their entries on Munich's Naturdenkmal oaks overlap directly with our Krüner Eiche (muc_002) and Reichs- und Friedenseiche (muc_003).

org: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliiton Uudenmaan piiri (Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, Uusimaa district)
why_them: The Helsinki region branch campaigns on protected natural monuments, which is what the King's Oak at the Pitkäkoski rapids (hel_001) and the Meilahti Ancient Pine by the Bronze Age burial cairn (hel_006) are, and both are photo gaps on our eight-tree Helsinki page.
